title: GPU NodeState Guardian Terraform module for Private VPC (ASG + Karpenter integration)
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module ("NodeState Guardian") to manage GPU node pools in Private VPC deployments. The module must support both ASG-backed and Karpenter-backed provisioning, provide safe rolling upgrades for GPU drivers and node AMIs, and include proactive health checks and lifecycle hooks to avoid noisy evictions during upgrades. This is intended for Dedicated/Private customers that run GPU inference pools and require deterministic behavior for upgrades and capacity fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Module exposes inputs for pool type (asg|karpenter), machine/instance profiles, GPU driver bundle version, golden AMI id, and desired capacity policies.
2) Upgrades perform a canary (2 nodes) verification run with automated eviction safeguards and automated rollback if GPU driver or kubelet health regressions are detected.
3) Health checks ensure nodes are tagged 'gpu-ready' only after driver + PCI bindings + nvidia-smi validation succeed.
4) Dual-autoscaler compatibility tested end-to-end: when ASG capacity is exhausted, Karpenter can be allowed to provision capacity (configurable).
5) Terraform plan = no destructive changes by default: node replacement uses lifecycle and create_before_destroy semantics where feasible.
6) Observability: per-pool Prometheus metrics for GPU-utilization, node upgrade progress, and drain failures; alerts documented.
7) Documentation and upgrade runbook added to Confluence and linked in module outputs.
tasks: Design input/variable schema and default values for both ASG and Karpenter modes
Implement lifecycle hooks: pre-drain validation, graceful cordon/drain, post-join validation
Add automated canary workflow (2 node canary) with smoke tests for inference container and GPU validation
Implement terraform-compliant upgrade flags and create_before_destroy where supported
Add provider-agnostic tagging and IAM role attachments for GPU workloads
Integrate Prometheus metrics exporters and expose scrapers in module outputs
Write full test matrix and CI pipeline for module (plan/apply/destroy in ephemeral envs)
Author runbook and rollback steps; add Confluence doc and links
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Initial design workshop with infra and runtime teams — agreed on 'node-state-ready' tagging and two-stage validation for driver install.
2026-02-24: Prototyped lifecycle hook scripts (bash + small Go binary) to run GPU driver validation and attach 'gpu-ready' tag only after success.
2026-02-28: Decision: use create_before_destroy on LaunchTemplate changes; full node replacement kept opt-in to avoid capacity shock for enterprise customers.
2026-03-02: Karpenter integration spike completed — confirmed Karpenter can be configured to respect pool-level taints/labels from the module.
2026-03-04: WIP: added terraform tests in CI using ephemeral account; first canary run failed due to driver install timeouts — increased timeout and added retries.
review_comments: PM (Sofia Patel): please ensure upgrade can be scheduled outside business hours via a start_window input.
Security (Noah Ibrahim): require explicit KMS ARN input for driver artifacts; disallow public S3 access for driver bundles.
Design (Eli Navarro): recommend module outputs include canonical node group dashboard links for Console.
Infra (Aria Park): request toggle to disable Karpenter fallback when Dedicated customers have strict capacity contracts.
testing_plan: CI pipeline executes matrix: [ASG-only, Karpenter-only, ASG+Karpenter-fallback] across zones with small and medium GPU instance types. Tests include: terraform plan checks, smoke inference job (curl/latency), driver validation (nvidia-smi), node drain/restore cycles, and metrics emission. Canary run is validated by automatic smoke test before proceeding to bulk replacement.
rollback_plan: If canary smoke tests fail, module sets an 'upgrade_failed' tag and aborts further replacements. Rollback strategy: revert to previous LaunchTemplate/AMI via terraform apply with a single-step replace disabled, and trigger automated node rejoin scripts. Runbook includes manual steps for forcing previous AMI when automatic rollback cannot complete.
observability_changes: Add per-module metrics: gpu_node_ready, gpu_driver_install_success, node_drain_failure_count, canary_upgrade_status. Dashboards: GPU Pool Health (per-pool GPU utilization + upgrade progress). Default alert: canary_upgrade_status != success for >15m triggers PagerDuty. Documented in release notes.
healthcheck_spec: Healthchecks run in three phases: pre-provision (quota/limits), post-provision (docker + nvidia-smi + inference smoke test), and runtime (periodic nvidia-smi + driver heartbeat). Nodes only receive 'gpu-ready' tag after all phases pass. Failures increment node_drain_failure_count and kick off automated retry with exponential backoff.
terraform_notes: Module will be published under github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/gpu-node-state-guardian with versioning following semantic versioning. Expose feature flags: enable_karpenter_fallback, create_before_destroy, canary_size, upgrade_schedule_cron. Provide example usage for private VPC with dedicated IAM role and KMS-protected driver artifacts.
implementation_risks:
1) Driver install timing varies across instance types and could delay upgrades; mitigated by adjustable timeouts and parallel installs.
2) Mixed autoscaler interactions may cause unexpected capacity spikes; mitigation: conservative defaults and explicit opt-in for Karpenter fallback.
3) Terraform provider limitations for certain resources requiring provider version pinning; include provider constraints in module documentation.
next_steps: Complete CI ephemeral environment tests, iterate on lifecycle script timeouts, add KMS validation per Security feedback, and schedule demo run with Platform QA the week of 2026-03-15.
